chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a man has two slave-sister-concubines, and he marries one of them, then decides to marry the second, it is not appropriate for him to marry the other until the first leaves his ownership, whether by him giving her as a gift or selling her. If he gives her as a gift to his son, that suffices for him.'

key_terms.اَلْأُخْتَانِ: two sisters (specifically slave sisters in this context)
key_terms.بَدَا لَهُ: it appeared to him / he decided
key_terms.يَهَبُهَا: he gives her as a gift

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for marrying two slave sisters in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific application of the Quranic prohibition against marrying two sisters simultaneously, extending it to the context of slave ownership where a man holds both in his possession. Shaykh al-Tusi records this to distinguish between the general marital restriction and the legal mechanics of transferring ownership, noting that gifting the first sister to one's son effectively removes her from the father's direct ownership, thereby permitting the marriage to the second. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the definition of 'possession' in the context of polygamy with slaves.
